model_output.score_comment_short: The accounting duties are clear, but their detail is limited.
model_output.score_comment_long: Month-end close, reconciliations, and audit assistance establish the accounting work you handle. Most bullets stop at the task, leaving the accounts, deliverables, and decisions unclear. Add those details to the current role first.
model_output.score_plain: A reviewer can identify your accounting background, but may have trouble distinguishing your work from similar staff accountant resumes. More detail about the close and audit would give them a better basis for comparison.
model_output.first_impression: Your move from Accounts Payable Clerk to Staff Accountant at Rivermark gives the work history a clear direction. The current role lists core accounting duties, but offers little detail about how you carry them out.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: "Responsible for month-end close tasks" does not identify the tasks you handle, so a reviewer cannot tell what part of the close is yours.
model_output.summary: Your work at Rivermark runs from vendor invoices and purchase order matching to journal entries, reconciliations, and fixed asset schedules. The sequence makes your accounting progression easy to follow and supports a staff accountant read. The annual audit bullet also shows involvement beyond routine transaction processing, though it doesn't say what you provide to auditors. That leaves a reviewer with only a broad view of your contribution.
strengths: Journal entries and account reconciliations show work directly relevant to a Staff Accountant role.
QuickBooks, NetSuite, and named Excel functions give a reviewer concrete tools to look for.
The accounting degree includes the school and completion year, making your education easy to verify.
gaps: The reconciliation bullet doesn't identify the accounts involved, making it difficult to understand the work's range.
Fixed asset schedules are listed without the updates or reviews you perform, so the responsibility remains broad.
The skills section doesn't connect either accounting system to a particular task, leaving their use in your work unclear.
